deleted.solution:
Let $\{G_\alpha\}_{\alpha \in I}$ be an arbitrary collection of open subsets of $\mathbb{R}$, and let

$$
G = \bigcup_{\alpha \in I} G_\alpha.
$$

To show that $G$ is open in $\mathbb{R}$, let $x \in G$ be arbitrary. By the definition of the union, there exists at least one index $\alpha_0 \in I$ such that $x \in G_{\alpha_0}$.

Since $G_{\alpha_0}$ is an open subset of $\mathbb{R}$, there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the open interval $(x - \varepsilon, x + \varepsilon)$ is contained in $G_{\alpha_0}$:

$$
(x - \varepsilon, x + \varepsilon) \subseteq G_{\alpha_0}.
$$

Because $G_{\alpha_0} \subseteq \bigcup_{\alpha \in I} G_\alpha = G$, it follows that

$$
(x - \varepsilon, x + \varepsilon) \subseteq G.
$$

Thus every point $x \in G$ is an interior point of $G$, which proves that $G = \bigcup_{\alpha \in I} G_\alpha$ is open in $\mathbb{R}$.
